name: Shay Boloor
zh_summary: @StockSavvyShay: 2026 feels like death by a thousand cuts for growth investors; the Iran war pushed oil and yields higher, a new inflation shock complicating the Fed, while businesses she owns keep executing despite falling stocks.
en_summary: @StockSavvyShay: 2026 feels like death by a thousand cuts for growth investors; the Iran war pushed oil and yields higher, a new inflation shock complicating the Fed, while businesses she owns keep executing despite falling stocks.
text:
2026 has honestly felt like death by a thousand cuts for growth investors because every time we get through one macro shock another one seems to show up. 

The Iran war has pushed oil prices and yields higher creating another inflation shock that's making Fed's job even harder while many of the businesses I own continue executing despite their stock prices telling a very different story. 

I think this is where the emotional tax of long-term investing really shows up because patience feels easy when your stocks are making new highs but it becomes a completely different animal when those same companies are suddenly down 50% or more.

The irony to me is that everyone wants to own the company that becomes a 20-year winner but very few people actually want the 20-year ownership experience.

Those returns rarely come in a straight line and I think some of my best portfolio decisions are made during periods like this when everything feels uncomfortable but long -term opportunity really hasn't changed.

en_summary: Adding to $ASTS during drawdown as rising yields do not change how early we are in building a larger space economy with satellites as another layer of global telecom infrastructure. AST has carrier partnerships accessing ~3B potential subscribers who prefer an alternative to $SPCX Starlink for direct-to-phone. Challenge is scaling to ~45 satellites and converting to paying users, but ~70% drawdown already reflects production and launch risk in valuation.
text:
I've been adding to my $ASTS position during this drawdown because rising yields don't change how early we are in building a much larger space economy where satellites become another layer of global telecom infrastructure.

AST already has carrier partnerships giving it access to ~3B potential subscribers and those carriers have every reason to support an alternative to Starlink rather than depend entirely on $SPCX for direct-to-phone connectivity.

The biggest challenge now is scaling to ~45 satellites and turning those partnerships into paying users but with the stock already in a ~70% drawdown I do think a lot of that production and launch risk is being reflected in valuation.

en_summary: $TSLA unveiled revamped Roadster at SpaceX facility using $SPCX thruster and suction tech to fly short distances, with 0-60 under 1 second. Estimate 2029 financial impact roughly $.06/share or 1.1% incremental to $5.40 consensus adj EPS assuming 3,000 deliveries/year and $100K unit profit. Halo effect on franchise more important. Remain cautious on $TSLA given extreme valuation (2026 P/E of 230x vs +45% long-term EPS growth), negative 2027-2030 earnings revisions, and unsupervised autonomy becoming commoditized.
text:
$TSLA unveiled its long-awaited revamped
Roadster EV last night before an invitation only audience at the SpaceX facility in McGregor TX.  The car, which leverages $SPCX thruster and suction technology to fly short distances, will offer promised acceleration from 0-60 in under 1 second, making it the fastest production car in the world. While amazing from an engineering and technology standpoint, we estimate the 2029 financial impact assuming 3,000 deliveries per year and a $100K unit profit per car, will be roughly $.06/share, or 1.1% incremental to 2029 consensus adj eps of $5.40.  More important is likely to be the halo effect on the Tesla franchise and brand impact created by the prototype's flight capabilities, acceleration and handling which could add far more incremental value from a franchise standpoint.   

We remain cautious on $TSLA given its extreme valuation (2026 P/E of 230x vs +45% long-term esp growth), negative 2027-2030 earnings revisions, and our view that unsupervised autonomy, the stock’s main value driver, will become increasingly commoditized over the next few years as full self-driving becomes table stakes for remaining in the automobile business. https://www.youtube.com/live/qt5p-_tE8d0?si=uniCV54KsS4Kfgvc
